🚑 Account Rescue: When Things Go Wrong · Lesson 6 of 6

Fake Pages, Extortion, Sextortion & Doxxing: Where Kenyans Report It

8 min read · Updated November 2026 · Free · Written for Kenya
Share: WhatsApp X Facebook Telegram LinkedIn

To stop an intimate image spreading on Facebook, Instagram and TikTok, StopNCII.org never asks you to upload the image. It creates a digital fingerprint on your own device, and participating platforms block matches.

Fake pages selling in your name, threats to leak photos, your home address posted in the comments: these feel like the end of the world, and extortionists count on that panic. You have more power than they want you to think. Platforms have dedicated routes, and Kenyan law is on your side.

1,463
victims identified in INTERPOL's Operation Contender 3.0 against social-media romance scams and sextortion in 14 African countries, including Kenya. They lost nearly USD 2.8M; 260 suspects were arrested (2025, via AllAfrica)

If someone is extorting you: the plan

  1. Stop replying. Don't pay. Paying proves you'll pay, and nothing stops them keeping copies.
  2. Preserve evidence before you block. Screenshot the profile with its username and link, the messages, any M-Pesa number or till, and the dates.
  3. Report in the app, then hash the images: stopncii.org if you were 18 or older in them, takeitdown.ncmec.org if you were under 18.
  4. Block and lock down. Set your accounts to private for now and check who can see your friends list.
  5. Report to the police. DCI's toll-free line is 0800 722 203, or WhatsApp 0709 570 000 (Fichua kwa DCI). Ask for an OB number.
  6. Tell one trusted person today. You don't have to handle this alone.
You are not the criminal here

Under Kenya's Computer Misuse and Cybercrimes Act, sharing someone's intimate images without consent can bring a fine of up to KES 200,000, two years in prison, or both (section 37). Cyber harassment (section 27, upheld by the courts in March 2026) carries up to KES 20 million or 10 years. Being targeted is not your shame.

Reporting fakes and abuse on each platform

PlatformRouteGood to know
InstagramProfile > ... > Report > pretending to be someone > Me. No access? help.instagram.com/contact/636276399721841The web form asks for a photo of your ID.
FacebookProfile > ... > Report profile > Pretending to be someone. No account? facebook.com/help/contact/295309487309948Use the same route for fake Pages selling in your name.
TikTokProfile > Share > Report > Pretending to be someoneBrands can also use tiktok.com/legal/report/Copyright for stolen content.
YouTubesupport.google.com/youtube/contact/impersonationThis includes AI copies of your face or voice, and names like 'Official' or 'Backup' added to yours.
XReport from the profile, or via help.x.com/en/safety-and-security/report-x-impersonationYou don't need an X account to report.
Intimate imagesstopncii.org (18+), takeitdown.ncmec.org (under 18)The hash is made on your device. The image never leaves it.

Kenyan routes beyond the apps

WhereContactUse it for
DCI (police)0800 722 203 toll-free; WhatsApp 0709 570 000Extortion, sextortion, impersonation fraud, threats
National KE-CIRT/CCincidents@ke-cirt.go.ke; +254 703 042700; ke-cirt.go.keCyber incidents: hacking, phishing, impersonation campaigns
Data Protection Commissioner (ODPC)odpc.go.ke/file-a-complaint; 020 780 1800Your personal data posted or misused, including doxxing by a business. ODPC says it investigates within 90 days.
Communications AuthorityComplain to your telco in writing first, then to the CA at ca.go.keTelco failures such as an unresolved SIM swap. The CA says it responds within 30 days.
EndaViralA ticket with your order ID from your accountFake 'EndaViral support' DMs. Real support never asks for passwords, codes or your M-Pesa PIN.

✅ Do this today (10 minutes)
⚡ Quick check

You want StopNCII.org to block an intimate image from spreading on Facebook, Instagram and TikTok. What do you have to send them?

StopNCII creates a hash, a numerical fingerprint, on your device. Participating platforms use it to detect and block matches. The image itself never leaves your phone.

🧠 Key takeaways
  1. Don't pay, and don't delete. Screenshot first, then report and block.
  2. Every major platform has an impersonation route, and some work without an account.
  3. StopNCII (18+) and Take It Down (under 18) block images without you uploading them.
  4. In Kenya: DCI for crimes, KE-CIRT for cyber incidents, ODPC for misuse of your data, and the CA when telcos don't act.
